newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania private oil firms try to prevent monopoly.
newsitem.headline: Romania private oil firms try to prevent monopoly.

text.p: Private oil and gas firms in Romania have founded a national company to counter what they say could become a monopoly by the state-run sector in the industry.

"The new company will encourage fair competition in the oil and gas sectors where private firms' interests have been poorly represented so far," Teodor Vostinaru, president of General Trading & Investments Co SA, told Reuters on Tuesday.
General Trading is a private oil products operator and one of the founders of the new company.

The new company, Petrogaz SA, is seen as a counter to a newly-created National Oil Company (CRO) which groups oil refineries and exploration, transport and distribution companies with majority state capital.
The National Oil Company's stated aim is to consolidate the state-run oil industry and ensure funds for crude imports badly needed in Romania's energy-starved industry.
"What Petrogaz plans to do in an early phase is buy 50 percent of Petrom's annual crude output, or some 3.5 million tonnes yearly, by offering attractive prices," Vostinaru said.
Petrom RA is Romania's sole oil exploration company.
Petrogaz also plans to take over administration of up to 49 percent of 58 firms which the CRO is managing.
"We are discussing the technical details of contracts allowing us to administer the privately-held 49 percent of these 58 companies," Vostinaru said.
"The 49 percent will give us a say in decision-making within the National Oil Company," he added.
Petrogaz has 30 Romanian private corporates and 30 individuals as founding members. They subscribed a capital of 550 billion lei, which will be paid over two years.
The company plans a public share offering later this year to further increase its capital. "We have had signs more companies are interested in joining us," said Vostinaru.

In the long run, Petrogaz will secure local and imported crude, oil products and gas supplies for local consumers. It will handle oil and gas processing and exports and will try to attract foreign investors to help oil and gas sector growth. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
